label: maxturns3-opus-high
claude_args: --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high --max-turns 3 --add-dir ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-review --add-dir ${{ github.workspace }}/../../_actions --setting-sources user --disallowedTools "Bash,Edit,Write,NotebookEdit,WebFetch,WebSearch,Read(//proc/**),Read(**/.git/**)" --json-schema '{"type": "object", "required": ["summary", "findings"], "additionalProperties": false, "properties": { "summary": {"type": "string"}, "findings": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object", "required": ["path", "line", "body"], "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}, "line": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1000000}, "body": {"type": "string"}}}}}}'
prompt:
You are reviewing pull request #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} as a code reviewer.
The PR's head is checked out in the working directory. Its diff against the base
branch is in ${{ runner.temp }}/claude-review/pr.diff.

You have at most 3 turns in total, and your answer must be one of them, so plan
your reads. Turn 1: read the diff and every source file it touches, all in one turn
as parallel Read calls. Turn 2, only if you need it: read, again in one turn of
parallel calls, the unchanged code the change calls or is called by, and the
repository's conventions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) where they bear on it. Then answer.
Never spend a turn on a single small read, and never use a turn without answering
when it is your last. Skip generated files, lockfiles, snapshots and recorded data.

Your review may be the only one this PR gets before it merges on its own, so be
thorough. For each change, ask what happens on the paths the author didn't test:
another event or trigger, a rerun, a skipped or cancelled job, a different actor
(a bot, an app, a person without write access), an empty, malformed or unusual
input (whitespace, tabs, Unicode, markup), a race between two runs. For GitHub
Actions workflows and merge gates, reason about how GitHub itself behaves: which
events fire, what a skipped or failed check does to a PR's mergeStateStatus, who
the actor is, what each token can do. The source of the actions this review runs on
is under ${{ github.workspace }}/../../_actions/<owner>/<repo>/<ref>; read it when a
pinned action's behaviour decides the answer. Where the behaviour of an action or
of GitHub decides it and you can't check it here, say what you're relying on.
Look hardest at code that decides whether something merges, releases or gets
permissions, and at text processing that turns input into rendered output.

Report every real problem a maintainer would want fixed or knowingly accepted
before merging: bugs, security issues, broken edge cases, missing or wrong tests,
and clear departures from the repository's conventions. Don't report style nits,
praise, or the PR's scope (what it bundles together is the author's call).

Every finding names a file path relative to the repository root and a line number
on the new side of that file, on a line the diff adds or shows as context: a finding
anywhere else holds the merge until the next push. When the problem lies in code the
diff doesn't touch, put the finding on the changed line that calls it, depends on it
or should have changed with it. Before you report a line, read it in the checked-out
file (not in the diff) and make sure it is the line the finding is about. Say what
goes wrong, in which situation, and how to fix it.

Answer with a short summary of the change and your verdict, and your findings.

findings.body:
**A PR can forge the review that unblocks its own merge.**

The gate now accepts any github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with `<!-- claude-review -->` as a review of the head. Every github-actions[bot] review on a same-repo PR comes from a `pull_request` workflow, which runs the PR branch's own workflow files and scripts.

`claude-review.yml` itself is one such workflow. It runs on `pull_request`, and its post job (`claude-review.yml:136-139`) checks out `.github/scripts` from the PR's merge ref. It then runs that copy of `post_claude_review.py` with `pull-requests: write`.

So a same-repo PR can do either of these:
- edit `post_claude_review.py` or `claude-review.yml`;
- add any workflow that runs `gh api .../reviews` with a body of `<!-- claude-review -->\nNo findings.`

The forged review lands on its own head. Once checks are green, PR Auto-Merge squash-merges it with no review at all. Copilot's review couldn't be forged this way. This file says outright that it uses `pull_request_target` so that "a PR can't edit the script that decides whether it merges". The marker check reopens exactly that hole for whoever pushes branches, including an agent like Sandcastle.

**Fix:** post from a trusted context. The review job stays on `pull_request`, writes the findings and head SHA to an artifact, and does nothing else. A separate `workflow_run`-triggered workflow then posts. It runs main's copy of the workflow and script and never executes PR code, the same pattern PR Review Submitted already uses. Even then, github-actions[bot] reviews from any other workflow carry no proof of origin. Either have PR Auto-Merge confirm that the marked review matches a successful Claude Review run from main for that head, or post under an identity a PR can't use (a GitHub App token held only by the posting workflow).

**A cancelled review on the same head can leave a failing check that stalls the PR.**

`cancel-in-progress: true` combined with the `labeled`, `ready_for_review` and `reopened` triggers recreates the problem this PR removes from `ci.yml` (lines 33-35). There, a `ready_for_review` run cancelled an in-progress run on the same head, and the cancelled check reported as a failure.

Here is how it happens:
1. `land.sh`/`reapply.sh` runs `gh pr ready` and adds `review:claude` within seconds of each other. Or a person removes and re-adds the label while a review is running. Or the PR is closed and reopened.
2. Two runs start on the same head, and the second cancels the first.
3. The cancelled "Review with Claude" check stays on the head commit, so mergeStateStatus is not CLEAN.
4. PR Auto-Merge (`pr-automerge.yml:306`) then waits until someone pushes again, even after the second run has posted a clean review.

I'm relying on the repo's own observation in `ci.yml` that a cancelled same-head check stays red; I couldn't check GitHub's rollup behaviour here.

**Fix:** don't let a same-head event cancel a run in progress. Either use `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event.action == 'synchronize' }}`, or add the head SHA to the group (`claude-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`) so only a new head supersedes it. Dropping `ready_for_review`/`reopened` alone isn't enough, because `labeled` can still race.

**The comment lines are checked against the wrong diff when the head moves before posting.**

`gh.pull_files(args.pr)` returns the PR's file diff as of now, at the current head. The review, though, is pinned to `commit_id = args.head`, the head at event time. The post job is in a separate concurrency group, so a push during the review job doesn't cancel it.

If the branch moves before posting, the commentable lines come from the new head's diff, while GitHub checks the comments against the old commit's diff. Two things can go wrong:
- A finding that sits on the old diff but not the new one is pushed into the body, and the job fails.
- A finding on a line that is only in the new diff is sent inline. GitHub then rejects the whole review with 422, so nothing is posted.

Neither case is covered by the tests.

**Fix:** take the commentable lines from the reviewed commit itself, using `GET repos/{repo}/compare/{base}...{head}` with the event's base and head SHAs, which is the same diff Claude reviewed. Or re-read the PR head first and skip posting with a notice if it no longer equals `--head`.

**`capture_output=True` throws away gh's error message, so post failures are hard to diagnose.**

With `capture_output=True` and `check=True`, a failed `gh api` call raises `CalledProcessError`, and its stderr is never printed. Example: GitHub answers 422 because one comment's line isn't in the diff, or because `commit_id` isn't on the PR. The job log then shows only `returned non-zero exit status 1`, not GitHub's response explaining which comment or field it rejected. The same applies to `pull_files`.

**Fix:** drop `capture_output` in `create_review`, since its stdout isn't used. Otherwise catch `CalledProcessError` in both calls and print `error.stderr` to stderr before exiting 1.

**Model output is put into a Markdown list item unescaped, so multi-line findings render broken.**

The line is `off_diff.append(f"- `{path}:{line}`: {body}")`. Claude's finding bodies are often several paragraphs, or contain a fenced code block, a heading or a list. Only the first line is inside the bullet. The next unindented paragraph or fence ends the list, so later findings show up as stray paragraphs and code blocks rather than a list of findings. A `path` containing a backtick also breaks the code span.

This is the review body a maintainer reads to see why the check is failing.

**Fix:** indent every continuation line of `body` by two spaces (`body.replace("\n", "\n  ")`). Wrap `path` in a code span longer than any backtick run inside it, as `release_post.py` does. Add a test with a multi-paragraph off-diff body.
